messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the prefix cache RFC — QA found a correctness edge with shared prefixes under eviction pressure, want to sync on a safe interface change.
jay: can you tl;dr the issue?
maria: tl;dr: when prefix entries are shared across routes, eviction can remove portions that other routes still expect to be resident. Our current owner/lease model only tracks a single owner per prefix shard, not multiple logical dependents.
oliver: ugh. is this about refcounts vs leases?
maria: yeah. Example: route A pins prefix "user:chat:ctx" then route B expects it too. If A releases because of inactivity but B is still serving, we evict and B breaks (KV miss + regen).
jay: do we have a repro?
maria: minimal repro in QA — created two clients sharing a long prefix, forced memory pressure with synthetic requests, saw stale KV misses that caused repeated regen loops.
kevin: is this about correctness or just perf? sounds correctness to me if requests fail or blow up.
maria: mostly correctness (wrong cache hits/misses) and availability (thundering re-generations). Also higher costs.
sasha: alternatives? refcounting per-prefix (increment when a route references), vs lease tokens with refresh, vs duplicating state per-tenant (no sharing).
jay: refcounting is straightforward but we need GC to avoid leaks if a route crashes. Leases solve crash safety but add refresh overhead.
maria: proposing an Owner API: pin_prefix(prefix, owner_id, ttl) -> returns lease_token. eviction respects active pins/leases. Also expose metrics: cache.pins.active, cache.pins.evicted_blocked_by_pin.
oliver: pragmatic: store a 16-bit pin_count in the prefix header per-shard. On pin, CAS increment. On release/expiry decrement. That keeps eviction fast.
sasha: CAS is doable but racey across shards. If we split prefixes across N shards need cross-shard atomicity?
kevin: we don't need cross-shard atomicity — pins are local to shard. But correctness invariant: pin_count>0 => not evict. If a route pinned across multiple prefixes and crash leaves some pins, the worst is leftover memory until TTL/GC.
maria: TTL is important. propose pins have TTL and background reclaimer that treats stale pins as released. Also have an occasional audit job to reconcile with active routes.
jay: what about metrics and alerting? We should know when pins prevent evictions frequently (memory pressure) and when stale pins accumulate.
maria: plan: add cache.pins.{total,by_prefix,stale_count,eviction_prevented} and an alert when stale_count / total > 5% for > 10m.
oliver: implementation concerns: per-prefix header increases metadata size; might affect hot-path allocation. We can pack pin_count + flags into existing header word.
sasha: test matrix: unit tests for CAS path, fuzz test for concurrent pin/release under eviction, chaos test where we kill route processes and ensure GC reclaims.
kevin: rollout: feature flag gated API, default off. Pilot with a small set of routes that already share prefixes. Canary in staging with synthetic memory pressure.
maria: migration: backfill existing prefixes with pin_count=0. No DB migration required. For routes that opt-in, they call pin_prefix at startup. We'll provide client SDK helpers to pin automatically when using shared prefix APIs.
jay: interface sketch: 
```
POST /cache/pin
{ prefix: "user:chat:ctx", owner: "route-A", ttl_s: 300 }
Response: { token: "abcd", expires_at: 1769200300 }
```
release: POST /cache/unpin { token }

Background reclaimer POST /cache/reclaim?cutoff=... responds with list of stale tokens removed
```

oliver: token-based model makes it easier to attribute pins and audit. TTL + refresh avoids long leaks.
sasha: agree. Also need a per-owner limit to avoid noisy tenants pinning everything. Quota check on pin endpoint.
maria: good call. quota metrics: pins.per_owner.active and pins.per_owner.evicted_attempts.
kevin: how about eviction policy change? LRU should ignore pinned prefixes, but we should still consider them for space accounting. If >80% of memory pinned, we need an emergency fallback (spill to disk or degrade model cache).
maria: add a graceful degradation path: if pinned_ratio > 80% then switch to conservative mode where we allow eviction of the oldest pins older than pin_ttl*0.5 with leaderboard and alert. This is a last-resort.
jay: ensure we log when we evict a pinned entry (should be extremely rare) with reason code.
sasha: testing: add e2e where we pin, then simulate memory spike and assert pinned entries stay resident and route continues. Also test crash + no-release -> GC reclaims after TTL.
maria: ops: dashboard with top prefixes by pin_count, top owners, memory used by pinned vs unpinned. Add a canary job that runs pin/unpin cycles.
kevin: security: pin API requires route identity, only internal services allowed. RBAC check in control plane.
maria: rollout steps: 1) API + header packing (behind FF) 2) metrics + dashboard 3) SDK helper + small pilot 4) canary with canary routes 5) broader opt-in
jay: timeline?
maria: spike + tests this week, impl next week, canary mid next sprint.
oliver: one more: consider async decrement path: instead of CAS on hot path, queue decrements to a per-shard background worker to amortize cost. Might reduce contention but increases window where count is stale.
sasha: background worker OK if TTL short. Need correctness proofs for eviction decision with eventual consistency.
maria: noted. I'll open a follow-up RFC PR with the API sketch, header packing options, and required tests. Will link to this thread.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime/prefix-pin-canary at 2026-04-06T15:00Z (refs #3452)
maria: thanks all, I'll post the RFC PR and assign reviewers. :thumbsup:
